title: Kebab barg
subtitle: Persian saffron-marinated lamb fillet skewers
excerpt: Kebab barg is the most prestigious Persian kebab: thin fillets of lamb leg marinated in saffron, onion, and olive oil, then grilled over charcoal or high heat. Barg means leaf, referring to the flat, wide shape of the meat on the skewer. Served with chelow and grilled tomatoes.
sourceNotes: Najmieh Batmanglij, Food of Life: Ancient Persian and Modern Iranian Cooking and Ceremonies (1986). Kebab barg documented as the centrepiece of Persian grilled meat culture. Margaret Shaida, The Legendary Cuisine of Persia (1992). The marinade, cutting technique, and cooking method described in detail.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate overnight for the best flavour. The meat keeps in the marinade in the fridge for up to 24 hours.
recipe.temperatureNote: The grill must be as hot as possible. Rest the skewers on the edge of the pan if using a griddle.

content.text: Kebab barg is the prestige Persian kebab: lamb leg cut into thin flat fillets, marinated for hours in saffron water, grated onion, and olive oil, then cooked fast over fierce heat. The saffron turns the meat a deep golden yellow and gives it a faintly floral, smoky character. The key is the cut: flat pieces about 1 cm thick and 5 cm wide thread onto skewers in a way that maximises contact with the heat.

items.prepNote: boneless, cut into thin flat fillets 1 cm thick
ground, dissolved in 3 tbsp hot water, cooled
coarsely grated, excess liquid squeezed out
dotted over the hot kebabs at serving

content.text: Put the dissolved {{saffron}} water into a bowl. Add squeezed {{onion}}, {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}}, lemon juice from {{lemon}}, {{sea-salt-fine}}, and {{black-pepper}}. Stir to combine.
Add the lamb fillets, turning to coat well. Cover and refrigerate for at least four hours, ideally overnight.
Take the meat out of the fridge 30 minutes before cooking. Thread the flat fillets on wide, flat metal skewers in a zigzag pattern so the meat lies flat against the skewer.

Heat the grill or griddle to the highest setting. Grill the kebabs for three to four minutes per side until well charred outside and still slightly pink within. Add the halved {{tomato}} alongside to grill at the same time.
Rest for five minutes. Dot {{unsalted-butter}} over the hot kebabs if using and scatter {{sumac}} over the grilled tomatoes. Serve with chelow.

items.symptom: The meat is dry and tough
items.cause: Lamb leg was cut too thin, or overcooked
items.fix: Barg fillets should be at least 1 cm thick. Pull off the heat when they still feel slightly springy.

items.symptom: The saffron colour is barely visible
items.cause: Saffron dissolved in water that was too cool, or poor-quality saffron
items.fix: Use boiling water to dissolve the saffron and cool completely before adding. The liquid should be a deep orange.

items.symptom: The meat falls off the skewer while cooking
items.cause: Skewers too thin or meat not threaded flat
items.fix: Wide, flat metal skewers grip the meat much better than thin round ones. Thread each fillet lengthways in a zigzag.

items.symptom: The onion flavour is too strong after marinating
items.cause: Too much onion or marinated for too long
items.fix: Squeeze all the liquid from the grated onion before adding. Marinate for no more than 24 hours.

content.text: Kebab barg (barg means leaf in Persian, referring to the flat shape) is the most prized kebab in Iran: ranked above koobideh (minced lamb) and joojeh (chicken). It is served at restaurants and at celebratory home meals. The classic service is barg alongside koobideh on one plate with chelow, grilled tomatoes, fresh herbs, and flatbread. This combination is called chelo kabab and is the national dish of Iran. The key flavour is saffron: Iran produces most of the world's saffron and uses it freely, especially in grilled dishes and rice.
